## Proof

Let $T = \mathbb{R}^2/\mathbb{Z}^2$ be the 2-torus and let $f = f(-\mathrm{id})$ be the homeomorphism induced by the matrix $-I = \begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}\in \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$. The mapping torus is
$$M = M(T,f) = (T\times[0,1])\,/\,(x,1)\sim(f(x),0).$$

### Step 1. Homology of $T$ and the induced map $f_*$

The homology of the 2-torus is
$$H_0(T)=\mathbb{Z},\quad H_1(T)=\mathbb{Z}^2,\quad H_2(T)=\mathbb{Z},\quad H_n(T)=0\ (n\ge 3).$$

The map $f:T\to T$ is $(x,y)\mapsto(-x,-y)$ on $\mathbb{R}^2/\mathbb{Z}^2$.

- On $H_0$: $f_*=\mathrm{id}$ (any continuous map of a path-connected space acts as the identity on $H_0$).
- On $H_1\cong\mathbb{Z}^2$: $f_*$ is exactly the matrix $-I$, i.e. $f_*=-\mathrm{id}$.
- On $H_2\cong\mathbb{Z}$: $f_*$ is multiplication by the degree of $f$. The degree is $\det(-I)=(-1)(-1)=+1$, so $f_*=\mathrm{id}$.

### Step 2. The short exact sequence (Wang sequence) for the mapping torus

The Wang long exact sequence for a mapping torus is
$$\cdots \longrightarrow H_q(T)\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{id}-f_*\;}H_q(T)\longrightarrow H_q(M)\longrightarrow H_{q-1}(T)\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{id}-f_*\;}H_{q-1}(T)\longrightarrow\cdots$$

Equivalently, for each $q$ there is a short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow \operatorname{coker}\!\big(\mathrm{id}-f_*:H_q(T)\to H_q(T)\big)\longrightarrow H_q(M)\longrightarrow \ker\!\big(\mathrm{id}-f_*:H_{q-1}(T)\to H_{q-1}(T)\big)\longrightarrow 0.$$

### Step 3. Compute $\mathrm{id}-f_*$ on each group

- **$H_0$**: $\mathrm{id}-f_* = \mathrm{id}-\mathrm{id}=0$. Hence $\ker=\mathbb{Z}$, $\operatorname{coker}=\mathbb{Z}$.
- **$H_1$**: $\mathrm{id}-f_*=\mathrm{id}-(-\mathrm{id})=2\,\mathrm{id}$ on $\mathbb{Z}^2$. This is injective, so $\ker=0$; and $\operatorname{coker}=\mathbb{Z}^2/2\mathbb{Z}^2\cong(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^2$.
- **$H_2$**: $\mathrm{id}-f_*=\mathrm{id}-\mathrm{id}=0$. Hence $\ker=\mathbb{Z}$, $\operatorname{coker}=\mathbb{Z}$.
- **$H_n$, $n\ge 3$**: the group is $0$, so both kernel and cokernel are $0$.

### Step 4. Assemble $H_q(M)$

**$q=0$:** $\operatorname{coker}(\mathrm{id}-f_*$ on $H_0)=\mathbb{Z}$, $\ker(\mathrm{id}-f_*$ on $H_{-1})=\ker$ on $0=0$.
$$H_0(M)\cong\mathbb{Z}.$$

**$q=1$:** $\operatorname{coker}(\mathrm{id}-f_*$ on $H_1)=(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^2$, $\ker(\mathrm{id}-f_*$ on $H_0)=\mathbb{Z}$. The short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^2\longrightarrow H_1(M)\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z}\longrightarrow 0$$
splits (since $\mathbb{Z}$ is free), giving
$$H_1(M)\cong\mathbb{Z}\oplus(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^2.$$

**$q=2$:** $\operatorname{coker}(\mathrm{id}-f_*$ on $H_2)=\mathbb{Z}$, $\ker(\mathrm{id}-f_*$ on $H_1)=\ker(2\,\mathrm{id}:\mathbb{Z}^2\to\mathbb{Z}^2)=0$. Thus
$$H_2(M)\cong\mathbb{Z}.$$

**$q=3$:** $\operatorname{coker}(\mathrm{id}-f_*$ on $H_3)=0$, $\ker(\mathrm{id}-f_*$ on $H_2)=\ker(0:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z})=\mathbb{Z}$. The short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow 0\longrightarrow H_3(M)\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z}\longrightarrow 0$$
gives
$$H_3(M)\cong\mathbb{Z}.$$

**$q\ge 4$:** both cokernel (on $H_q=0$) and kernel (on $H_{q-1}=0$) vanish, so
$$H_q(M)=0,\qquad q\ge 4.$$

### Step 5. Consistency check

$M$ is a closed 3-manifold (a torus bundle over $S^1$), so $H_q(M)=0$ for $q>3$, consistent with the computation. The Euler characteristic (using free ranks $1,1,1,1$) is
$$\chi(M)=1-1+1-1=0,$$
which agrees with the general fact that $\chi=0$ for any mapping torus (it fibers over $S^1$). The torsion $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^2\subset H_1$ does not affect $\chi$.

### Result

$$\boxed{\begin{aligned}
H_0\!\big(M(T,f(-\mathrm{id}))\big)&\cong\mathbb{Z},\\
H_1\!\big(M(T,f(-\mathrm{id}))\big)&\cong\mathbb{Z}\oplus(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^2,\\
H_2\!\big(M(T,f(-\mathrm{id}))\big)&\cong\mathbb{Z},\\
H_3\!\big(M(T,f(-\mathrm{id}))\big)&\cong\mathbb{Z},\\
H_n\!\big(M(T,f(-\mathrm{id}))\big)&=0\quad\text{for }n\ge 4.
\end{aligned}}$$
